title: In-Storage Acceleration of Retrieval Augmented Generation as a Service
problem: As RAG deployments shift knowledge bases to persistent NVMe storage to handle ever-growing corpora, the Search & Retrieval phase — comprising embedding model inference, similarity/relevance search over dynamic data structures, and long-latency storage accesses — becomes the dominant bottleneck for end-to-end latency.
motivation: Moving RAG knowledge bases from DRAM to persistent storage dramatically lowers cost but fundamentally reshapes the performance profile, making in-storage compute an essential architecture to avoid the retrieval bottleneck from penalizing LLM generation quality of service.
method: The paper embeds a reconfigurable processor directly inside NVMe storage devices that can reprogram itself to work with different search algorithms (like HNSW or IVF, which organize vectors to speed up matching). This in-storage processor runs the smaller language models that convert search queries into vectors entirely inside the storage—without the main CPU getting involved. It also performs the similarity search to find relevant documents, all without data leaving the storage device. The main GPU (DGX A100) only participates once documents are selected, to generate the final answer.
key_novelty: An in-storage processor that reconfigures itself to run both query-to-vector conversion and document search entirely inside the storage device, eliminating slow data transfers between storage and the CPU.
contributions: Empirical analysis identifying Search & Retrieval as the dominant RAG latency contributor when using persistent storage
Metamorphic in-storage accelerator architecture supporting diverse RAG algorithms and dynamic data structures
In-storage execution of smaller language models for query embedding generation
Up to 4.3x end-to-end throughput improvement over Xeon CPU + NVMe and 1.5x over A100 GPU + DRAM pipelines

metrics.speedup: 4.3x over Xeon CPU + NVMe; 1.5x over A100 GPU + DRAM

limitations: In-storage embedding model execution is limited to smaller language models; large LLM generation still offloaded to external GPU systems.
primary_theme: in-storage accelerator for RAG retrieval and embedding
